title: Lighthouse Reef and the Great Blue Hole

briefing.summary: Cross the shallow Lighthouse Reef platform and survey its steep eastern and western edges around the Great Blue Hole.
facts: The Great Blue Hole is 318 m across and about 124 m deep; it sits inside Lighthouse Reef atoll.
The reef platform stays shallow for kilometres before dropping sharply into deeper water on either side.
With a surface start you begin over the eastern slope, facing west toward the reef.
Lighthouse Reef is part of the Belize Barrier Reef Reserve System, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
hazards: Shallow reef structure near the rim -- watch your depth and avoid contact with coral.
A steep drop-off from the reef flat to open ocean; currents can be stronger there.
Total darkness below a few hundred metres on the outer slope; only your lights work.
Your Class B hull is rated to 6,500 m, clearing the deepest cell in this survey.

objectives.title: Survey the eastern atoll drop-off
objectives.hint: The eastern atoll drop-off lies east of the hole, where the seabed falls to about 200 m.

objectives.title: Survey the western atoll drop-off
objectives.hint: The western atoll drop-off lies west of the hole, where the reef flat steepens toward 200 m.
